title: Point the emitter
summary: Collect the light of a point emitter in the Output detector on the left. The emitter sends light in all directions. You may place one curved piece of silver, shaped like a lens, in the marked region. The score is the share of the emitter's power that reaches Output. Power that the silver absorbs counts as given off.
hints: Light that leaves the emitter towards the right is lost. A silver shell behind the emitter can reflect it back.
A curved mirror turns light from a point at its focus into a parallel beam. The focus is half the radius of curvature away from the mirror.

Make both faces of the lens shape curve the same way, so that it is a thin shell, put it to the right of the emitter with its hollow side facing the emitter, and choose the radius so that the emitter sits at the focus.

goal.text: Send as much of the emitter's power as possible into Output
